challenges.claim: The device note's Asaph parenthetical mislabels the collection, and its count corresponds to no object the row names: it calls Psalm 79 one of 'the five Asaph psalms' while identifying that set as '(Ps.73-83, mizmor le-asaph)', a range of 11 psalms whose superscriptions are not uniformly mizmor le-Asaph.
challenges.evidence: psalm_device_inventory.json genre_label_membership.le_asaph = [50, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 78, 79, 80, 81, 82, 83] = 12 psalms book-wide; the range the row names, Ps.73-83, is 11 psalms; neither figure is five, and the row supplies no swept object for 'five'. The label is wrong for 3 of those 11: genre_label_membership.mizmor omits 74, 78 and 81, and the bytes agree - oshb:Ps.74.1 opens מַשְׂכִּ֗יל לְאָ֫סָ֥ף (web:Ps.74.0 = oshb:Ps.74.1, identity psalm; WEB title “A contemplation by Asaph.”), oshb:Ps.78.1 opens on the same 2-token label (web:Ps.78.0 = oshb:Ps.78.1, identity), and oshb:Ps.81.1 tokenizes to 4 words of which the last is לְאָסָֽף and 0 is a mizmor token (web:Ps.81.0 = oshb:Ps.81.1, shift +1; WEB title “For the Chief Musician. On an instrument of Gath. By Asaph.”). Sweep of the contiguous formula, skeleton מזמור לאסף: 7 verses book-wide (oshb:Ps.50.1, Ps.73.1, Ps.75.1, Ps.76.1, Ps.79.1, Ps.82.1, Ps.83.1), i.e. 6 verses inside Ps.73-83 against 11 psalms in the range; oshb:Ps.77.1 and oshb:Ps.80.1 invert the order to לְאָסָ֥ף מִזְמֽוֹר and לְאָסָ֣ף מִזְמֽוֹר respectively. A repair should name the swept object and its unit (le-Asaph psalms vs mizmor-labelled psalms) instead of blending them.

challenges.claim: Row prose carries two campaign-process references banned by the standing register purge: a file-order row reference in the rationale and a writer-part reference in device_notes.
challenges.evidence: The rationale reads 'every row below answers to that one parent' and device_notes reads 'that this part carries through to the collection's final psalm at Psalm 83'. The standing rules forbid file-order talk and positional row references in row prose outright and require cross-row references to be verse-anchored (the seam form, e.g. 79:4|79:5). Both phrases are removable without touching the parent claim, which is itself correct: web_mt_offset_map.json psalms.79 gives one 13-verse psalm, and check_tiling reports 13 of 13 verses covered by 3 rows with no gaps or overlaps.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.79.5-Ps.79.9. The opening seam is sound and byte-verified: oshb:Ps.79.5 opens עַד מָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה, an unambiguous vocative of the divine name, and WEB agrees (“How long, Yahweh? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy burn like fire?” web:Ps.79.5). Both Hebrew runs collate at byte tier. Ps 79 is an identity psalm, so the row's web:/oshb: pairings need no offset arithmetic and are correct as written. The closing seam at 79:9|79:10 also survives - oshb:Ps.79.10 does open a fresh interrogative, and that particle is a recurrent book-wide restart (sweep: 10 verses open on a token whose skeleton is למה) - but the row reaches the right seam through a wrong description of it, and it does not disclose a vocative sitting inside its own span. With a live and unaddressed rival at 79:8|79:9, 'high' confidence sits at the top of its defensible range. I do not contest the span.

challenges.claim: The device note bounds this psalm's strophes by 'the two vocative restarts' at web:Ps.79.5 and web:Ps.79.10, but oshb:Ps.79.10 contains no vocative, while a genuine vocative sits undisclosed inside the row's own span at oshb:Ps.79.9.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.79.10 opens לָ֤מָּה יֹאמְר֣וּ - an interrogative particle plus a 3mp prefix-conjugation verb - and its only divine-name token is אֱֽלֹהֵ֫יהֶ֥ם, the 5th of 13 tokens, a 3mp-suffixed form standing inside the nations' reported speech, which WEB renders “Why should the nations say, “Where is their God?”” (web:Ps.79.10): speech about a deity, not address to one. Conversely oshb:Ps.79.9 opens עָזְרֵ֤נוּ אֱלֹ֘הֵ֤י יִשְׁעֵ֗נוּ, an imperative plus a genuine vocative, rendered “Help us, God of our salvation, for the glory of your name. Deliver us, and forgive our sins, for your name’s sake.” (web:Ps.79.9). Under the cross-seam cohesion rule that in-span vocative both undercuts the 'bounded by vocative restarts' framing and leaves a rival seam at 79:8|79:9 that rejected_alternative never reaches - it considers only extension through web:Ps.79.13. The 79:9|79:10 seam should be rewarranted on the interrogative restart, which is what the text actually supplies.

challenges.claim: The signal calling web:Ps.79.6-9 'an unbroken imperative chain' is falsified inside that range, and one of the four links it names is not an imperative form.
challenges.evidence: 1 of the 4 verses named, web:Ps.79.7, carries no volitive of any kind: oshb:Ps.79.7 reads in full כִּ֭י אָכַ֣ל אֶֽת יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְֽאֶת נָוֵ֥הוּ הֵשַֽׁמּוּ - a causal clause with suffix-conjugation verbs - which WEB renders “for they have devoured Jacob, and destroyed his homeland.” (web:Ps.79.7). The link glossed 'don't hold' is oshb:Ps.79.8's אַֽל תִּזְכָּר, a prohibitive built on the prefix conjugation rather than an imperative form; the staged extract carries no morphology layer, so this is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses, and WEB's “Don’t hold the iniquities of our forefathers against us. Let your tender mercies speedily meet us, for we are in desperate need.” (web:Ps.79.8) does not distinguish the two. 'Interrupted by a causal clause at web:Ps.79.7' would state the same cohesion argument truthfully. Toolkit note: check_universals does not flag 'unbroken' - its lexicon covers no/every/all/none but no continuity adjective.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.79.10-Ps.79.13. Every claim re-derives. The opening warrant is byte-true: oshb:Ps.79.10 begins לָ֤מָּה יֹאמְר֣וּ, and a sweep of verse-initial tokens whose skeleton is למה returns 10 verses book-wide (oshb:Ps.2.1, Ps.10.1, Ps.44.25, Ps.49.6, Ps.68.17, Ps.74.11, Ps.79.10, Ps.80.13, Ps.88.15, Ps.115.2), so the interrogative restart is a recurrent tier-1 discourse signal rather than an ad hoc reading. The K/Q disclosure is exactly right against the inventory: pmarks_Ps.json kq carries one note at Ps.79.10 (65 verses / 68 notes book-wide), and the verse tokenizes with the unpointed ketiv and the pointed qere adjacent, בגיים בַּגּוֹיִ֣ם, the documented inline-ketiv pattern; the row names them in the correct order. The device note is correct against the inventory too: book_boundary_doxologies places Book III's close at MT Ps.89.53 = WEB 89:52, later than this psalm, and five_books puts Book III at 73-89, so web:Ps.79.13's vow is the psalm's own close and not a book doxology. check_web_quotes checked 36 curly quotes across this cluster and flagged 8, 0 of them in this row; the row's 4 Hebrew runs collate at byte tier (collate.py). Confidence 'medium' is well calibrated: the 79:12|79:13 rival is live - oshb:Ps.79.13 opens on waw plus an independent 1cp pronoun, WEB “So we, your people and sheep of your pasture, will give you thanks forever. We will praise you forever, to all generations.” (web:Ps.79.13) - and rejected_alternative names and answers it. Two observations, neither filed. First, the K/Q gloss 'the word for nations' is imprecise: the non-K/Q token הַגּוֹיִם֮ stands earlier in the same verse and the K/Q sits on the prepositional pair, so the gloss alone does not disambiguate - the quoted bytes do. Second, citation_sweep raises two prose warns that this row's rationale and first signal bind Hebrew to a K/Q verse without in-field K/Q disclosure; the disclosure is present in the second signal and the quoted span excludes the K/Q token, so those are informational, not defects.

Span Ps.80.1-Ps.80.3. Ps 80 is a shift +1 psalm (web_mt_offset_map.json psalms.80: rule 'shift', k 1, mt_title_verses [1]), so every original-language cite needs dual-cite arithmetic, and all 5 pairings in boundary_evidence_refs are correct: web:Ps.80.1 = oshb:Ps.80.2, web:Ps.80.3 = oshb:Ps.80.4, web:Ps.80.7 = oshb:Ps.80.8, web:Ps.80.19 = oshb:Ps.80.20, with the title pseudo-ref web:Ps.80.0 = oshb:Ps.80.1 in the owner-ruled form. Both Hebrew runs collate at byte tier. The two counted claims re-derive exactly: oshb:Ps.80.4 tokenizes to 5 space-separated words (אֱלֹהִ֥ים הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נוּ וְהָאֵ֥ר פָּ֝נֶ֗יךָ וְנִוָּשֵֽׁעָה), so 'a five-word Hebrew form of the refrain' is exact, and its divine name is אֱלֹהִ֥ים alone, as the second signal says. A skeleton sweep of השיבנו returns 3 verses book-wide - oshb:Ps.80.4, Ps.80.8, Ps.80.20 - all inside this psalm and mapping to web:Ps.80.3, web:Ps.80.7, web:Ps.80.19, so 'returns 3 times' is exact in verses and the three refs are the right ones. Reading the refrain as closing rather than opening its unit is the choice rejected_alternative names, and it is defensible: nothing in the bytes at 80:3|80:4 favours the other cut, since oshb:Ps.80.5 opens its own fresh divine-name address (יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים צְבָא֑וֹת). Confidence 'high' is earned. One observation, not filed: the rationale quotes רֹ֘עֵ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל הַאֲזִ֗ינָה but glosses it “Shepherd of Israel, you who lead Joseph like a flock, you who sit above the cherubim, shine out.”…“shine out.” (web:Ps.80.1); WEB fronts its rendering of the quoted third token as “Hear us, Shepherd of Israel, you who lead Joseph like a flock, you who sit above the cherubim, shine out.”, so 2 of the 3 quoted Hebrew tokens are rendered inside the glossed span and 1 is not, while the gloss's final words render הוֹפִֽיעָה, token 9 of 9 in oshb:Ps.80.2 and therefore inside the Hebrew quote's elided tail. Both sides are ellipsis-disclosed and scoped to the same verse, so this is a quote/gloss recut opportunity rather than a defect.

Span Ps.80.4-Ps.80.7. All 4 refs carry the right +1 arithmetic and both Hebrew runs collate at byte tier. The opening warrant is byte-true and genuinely verse-initial: oshb:Ps.80.5 begins יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים צְבָא֑וֹת, which WEB renders “Yahweh God of Armies, how long will you be angry against the prayer of your people?” (web:Ps.80.4). The close is the second of exactly 3 refrain returns (skeleton השיבנו: 3 verses book-wide, oshb:Ps.80.4/8/20), and its quoted Hebrew matches oshb:Ps.80.8 byte for byte including the וְהָאֵ֥ר that the third return drops. Confidence 'high' is earned: a refrain-bounded unit with 0 rival seams inside its 4 verses. One contract defect. Observation, not filed: device_notes speaks of 'the fuller divine name that the refrain itself adopts on its second and third returns', but the complaint's name at oshb:Ps.80.5 is the 3-token form and is byte-identical (collate tier byte) to 1 of the 3 returns, the third at oshb:Ps.80.20, the second at oshb:Ps.80.8 carrying the 2-token form; read as the tsevaot expansion the sentence is true, so I do not file it, but the definite description is looser than the bytes.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.80.8-Ps.80.13. The mark disclosure is the best evidence in the row and is exactly right: pmarks_Ps.json suspended holds the single entry keyed Ps.80.14, so 'the one such mark recorded in this book's inventory' is exact at 1; the dual-cite web:Ps.80.13 = oshb:Ps.80.14 is the correct +1 arithmetic, and the 'single-witness' plus seg-layer caveat matches the toolkit's handling. The refrain-absence claim re-derives as true: a skeleton sweep of השיבנו puts 0 of the 3 book-wide returns inside oshb:Ps.80.9-14. Both Hebrew runs collate at byte tier and the closing quote matches oshb:Ps.80.14 exactly. The seam at 80:13|80:14 is right and confidence 'medium' is well calibrated. But one of the row's two register signals misdescribes the text, an in-span rival seam goes unaddressed, and the rival-rejection warrant is unmirrored.

This is the shared seam at 80:13|80:14, argued from the far side as well, so under the seam-pair rule the cure is authored once and installed on both sides in the same pass - and the far-side statement of that seam is itself byte-defective, so one edit should carry both fixes.

challenges.claim: The signal calling web:Ps.80.12-13 'still indicative' is false at web:Ps.80.12, which opens on the same verse-initial interrogative this cycle elsewhere treats as seam-seating, leaving a rival seam at 80:11|80:12 that rejected_alternative never addresses.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.80.13 (= web:Ps.80.12, shift +1) opens לָ֭מָּה פָּרַ֣צְתָּ - interrogative particle plus a 2ms suffix-conjugation verb, a question put to the addressee, not an indicative - and WEB agrees: “Why have you broken down its walls, so that all those who pass by the way pluck it?” (web:Ps.80.12). Sweep: 10 verses book-wide open on a token whose skeleton is למה (oshb:Ps.2.1, Ps.10.1, Ps.44.25, Ps.49.6, Ps.68.17, Ps.74.11, Ps.79.10, Ps.80.13, Ps.88.15, Ps.115.2), and both oshb:Ps.79.10 and oshb:Ps.80.13 are in that list. Since the same verse-initial particle at web:Ps.79.10 is treated in this cycle as strong enough to seat a strophe seam, its occurrence at web:Ps.80.12 is a rival seam inside this span; the row may still prefer to keep the vine figure whole through web:Ps.80.13, but it has to say so rather than describe the verse as indicative.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.80.14-Ps.80.19. The refrain-progression analysis is the strongest evidence in the cluster and it re-derives exactly: oshb:Ps.80.4 / Ps.80.8 / Ps.80.20 tokenize to 5 / 6 / 7 words with divine-name heads of 1 / 2 / 3 tokens, so the stated 1-2-3 progression is byte-true. The waw finding is byte-true and genuinely informative: the standalone token הָאֵ֥ר spliced from oshb:Ps.80.20 matches as a whole token only there, while oshb:Ps.80.4 and oshb:Ps.80.8 read וְהָאֵ֥ר; a byte search on the 3-word tail spliced from oshb:Ps.80.20 hits 3 verses (oshb:Ps.80.4, Ps.80.8, Ps.80.20) whereas the tail spliced from oshb:Ps.80.4, which carries the waw, hits 2 (oshb:Ps.80.4, Ps.80.8). The row's 4 Hebrew runs collate at byte tier, all 5 refs carry correct +1 arithmetic, and the closing quote matches oshb:Ps.80.20 at byte tier. The absence claim in rejected_alternative re-derives as true (no vocative and 0 refrain returns between oshb:Ps.80.16 and Ps.80.19). writer_attempt_id_as_delivered is a logged normalization and I treat it as such. Confidence 'high' is earned on the close. Both challenges are in how the evidence is stated, not in the span.

challenges.claim: The gloss attached to the waw-less refrain verb supplies the very conjunction the same sentence correctly says the verse drops, and it is presented in curly quotes although no WEB text reads that way.
challenges.evidence: The fourth signal glosses oshb:Ps.80.20's הָאֵ֥ר as 'and cause...to shine' while asserting 'no conjunctive waw' in the same parenthesis. WEB reads “Turn us again, Yahweh God of Armies. Cause your face to shine, and we will be saved.” (web:Ps.80.19) - the clause begins 'Cause', with no coordinating conjunction before it; the verse carries 1 occurrence of the word 'and', standing before the final clause, where it renders the waw of וְנִוָּשֵֽׁעָה. check_web_quotes flags the field ('curly quote with NO web: ref in its field'), so the string is neither verifiable as WEB nor consistent with the row's own finding. The waw contrast itself is correct and should be kept; only the gloss needs recutting to the WEB rendering of the token actually quoted.

challenges.claim: The first signal dual-cites web:Ps.80.14 = oshb:Ps.80.15 and then says the verse 'opens with the petition verb cluster', which is true of WEB word order only and false of the MT verse it cites - and the misdescription costs the row the strongest tier-1 warrant available at its own opening seam.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.80.15's first two tokens are אֱלֹהִ֣ים צְבָאוֹת֮, a vocative, with the verb pair שֽׁ֫וּב נָ֥א following as tokens 3 and 4; WEB inverts the order, “Turn again, we beg you, God of Armies. Look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vine,” (web:Ps.80.14). The MT verse therefore opens on a divine-name vocative restart - the same signal class this cycle treats as tier-1 elsewhere in the cluster (oshb:Ps.79.5 עַד מָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה, and the post-title vocative of oshb:Ps.79.1) - not on a verb contrast with the refrain. Stating it correctly strengthens rather than weakens the seam at 80:13|80:14; under the seam-pair rule the correction belongs on both sides of that seam in the same pass.
